title: The officer who fired is cleared
article: The Saguenay police officer who fatally shot the occupant of a dwelling in La Baie in February 2012 has been cleared by the police investigation.
The family of Mikel Dallaire, 24, was officially informed on Friday morning that no criminal charges will be laid against the officer in question.
The victim's mother and sister are dissatisfied with the explanations provided.
The case goes back to February 28, 2012, at 1 a.m. Five armed Saguenay police officers responded to a distress call.

Mikel Dallaire, 23, holding two knives, had taken refuge in the bathroom with his partner at the time. The woman swore she was not being threatened by the man, but he was shot dead with three bullets.
Seventeen months after the events, Dallaire's sister and mother were informed that no charges would be brought against the officer or officers responsible for the gunfire.

"Each officer reacts in their own way. It depends on the person. There's kind of a gray area, and they move from one area to another," summarized the victim's sister, Amélie Dallaire, and his mother, Christine Allard.

The investigator reportedly added that the ex-partner who witnessed the incident had changed her version of events several times. But according to the family members, the woman had always maintained the same account: that night, Dallaire was dangerous only to himself.
"It was himself he wanted to harm. Deep down, it was a cry for help, but they didn't understand it," said the two women in unison.

The two women called the conclusion of the Director of Criminal and Penal Prosecutions unfair. They are still seeking answers to their two most important questions: why did the officers not first attempt to subdue the man, and why, after firing two bullets into his leg, did they fire a third into his stomach?
"I am certain the third bullet was too much," said the mother. "That's the one that was fatal. It seems to me that police officers have techniques to disarm someone without killing them."
The family is now awaiting the coroner's report before deciding whether to pursue civil action against the officers, the municipal police, and the City of Saguenay.
"An accident, an illness, I could have understood," said the mother. "But to lose a child in this way, I will never understand."
The coroner's report is expected to be completed in the fall.
